original_question: Let G be a locally-finite simple geodetic graph and let t be a natural number. If C is an embedded cycle whose diameter exceeds t and whose length is minimal among all such paths in G, must C contain a geodesic subpath of length t + 1?
target_in_paper: Section D (Open Problems Related to Computer Science), unnumbered open problem/conjecture on minimal embedded cycles in locally-finite simple geodetic graphs.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's target. It has the correct graph class (locally-finite, simple, geodetic), the correct parameter t in N, the correct minimality hypothesis (minimum length among cycles of diameter exceeding t), and the correct conclusion (existence of a geodesic subpath of length t + 1).
missing_details: The minimality clause should be made explicit as ranging over all embedded cycles in G with diameter exceeding t; the paper's wording says 'such paths', but the intended object is the cycle/circuit itself.
To be fully stand-alone, 'embedded cycle' should be defined as a cycle with no repeated vertices other than the initial/final vertex.
The diameter condition should be clarified as referring to the diameter of the vertex set of C measured in the ambient graph metric of G, not the intrinsic metric of the cycle.
The paper's notion of length is the number of edges, so that convention should be stated.
A 'geodesic subpath of length t + 1' should be clarified to mean a contiguous subpath of C with t + 1 edges that is a shortest path in G between its endpoints.
If full self-containment is desired, it is worth stating that the paper works with simple undirected graphs.
The convention for N is not explicitly fixed in the note, so one may specify that t is a positive integer if that convention matters.
refined_question: Let G be a locally finite simple geodetic graph, and let t be a natural number. Suppose C is an embedded cycle in G (that is, a cycle with no repeated vertices except its initial/final vertex) such that the diameter of V(C), measured in the graph metric of G, is greater than t, and such that C has minimum length among all embedded cycles in G whose diameter is greater than t. Must C contain a contiguous subpath with t + 1 edges that is a geodesic in G?
justification: The draft is already almost a verbatim restatement of the open problem reproduced in arXiv:2202.10663. I kept the scope exactly there: locally-finite simple geodetic graphs, a minimal-length embedded cycle of diameter exceeding t, and the conclusion that such a cycle should contain a geodesic subpath of length t + 1. The only refinements were to remove the obvious 'such paths' slip, and to make explicit the background conventions on embedded cycles/circuits, path length, and the metric meaning of diameter so that the question is fully stand-alone without broadening it to neighboring results about bounded embedded-circuit diameter or plain groups.
